newsitem.title: USA: GE growth prospects impress analysts.
newsitem.headline: GE growth prospects impress analysts.

text.p: General Electric Co appears set to ride its well-oiled profit machine through 1997 with only a few minor potholes seen on the road ahead.
"There's not a lot on the horizon that could result in a negative surprise," Bill Fiala, capital goods analyst at Edward D. Jones in St. Louis, said on Thursday.
In an indication of its financial strength, GE earlier Thursday boosted its quarterly dividend, increased the size of its share repurchase program and announced a 2-for-1 stock split.

"The fact that they continue to repurchase shares and support internal growth and make a number of sizable acquisitions -- and increase their dividend -- just reinforces that GE has a very strong cash flow," Fiala said.
The analyst said the diversified Fairfield, Conn.-based group should experience annual earnings growth of 12 percent during the next five years.
"We have not even begun to see the tip of the iceberg in terms of GE's potential growth," said Nicholas Heyman, vice president of research at NatWest Securities Corp.
Heyman said GE's compounded earnings per share growth could swell to 17.6 percent from 1996 to 2000, from 11.2 percent from 1991 to 1995.
"Those are heady numbers for a company this size," he said, adding that the increase was driven by actual sales growth as opposed to operating margin improvement.

Working in GE's favor is its push to expand all its businesses outside the United States, its shift to sell more services to existing manufacturing and equipment customers, and its emphasis on improved production quality, Heyman said.
"The magic of this company is the diversification, and the market seems to be willing to pay for that," one Wall Street analyst said.
GE has major businesses in power generators, appliances, lighting, plastics, medical systems, aircraft engines, financial services and broadcasting.

The Wall Street analyst said GE has a penchant for tight control, as reflected in the stock buyback and dividend increase. "People can get a little distressed at GE's control, but the bottom line is that only good companies are able to exercise control," she said.

"GE has good prospects in many global markets and a management philosophy that they are never satisfied with what they have, which is healthy," said Steve O'Neil, vice president at J.J.B. Hilliard-W.L. Lyons in Louisville, Kentucky.
"They are so diversified that it's hard to think of a single event that could affect all their businesses in a specific way," O'Neil said.
A GE spokesman told Reuters on Thursday that the company was on track to meet analysts' expectations of $7.2 billion to $7.3 billion in earnings this year.
That would represent the the highest profit of any company in the United States, the first time GE would achieve that distinction.
"We obviously have good strong momentum," said GE spokesman Bruce Bunch. "I think we'll see continued good growth."
Bunch declined to give specific projections.
One Wall Street analyst said broadcasting was a potential pitfall for GE, which owns the NBC television network.
"The network business is cyclical, and GE can't rely on the fact that ABC and CBS will be asleep at the switch forever," she said.
Plastics, increasingly a commodity industry, could also present the company with difficulties because pricing is beyond the control of manufacturers, the analyst added.
